title: Speculative prefetch + delta-encoded prefix deduplication for prompt cache
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: reduce redundant KV cache loads and GPU memory footprint for hot prompt prefixes by combining speculative prefetching at the batching layer with a lightweight delta-encoding + canonicalization step to dedupe similar prefixes across concurrent requests. This ticket scopes an implementation that is safe for production: non-blocking, opt-in by route, and reversible (feature flag + circuit breaker).

Background: continuous batching often aggregates requests that share substantial prefix overlap (repeated system + instruction templates, repeated user history excerpts, or multi-tenant apps sending identical preambles). Serving runtime today treats each request prefix as a separate cache key which triggers duplicate KV cache materialization and increases GPU resident memory. Upstream work (various prefix-fragment pooling tickets) reduced some redundancy but we still observe 12-18% wasted GPU memory and 7-11% extra token compute on a few enterprise workloads.

Proposal (high level):
1) Speculative prefix prefetch: when dispatcher sees an incoming batch with multiple requests, compute a quick locality fingerprint (rolling window Rabin fingerprint + 64-bit siphash) across prompt tokens and rank prefix candidates for prefetch. Prefetch runs asynchronously to the main decode thread with a bounded worker pool.
2) Delta-encoded canonicalization: canonicalize prefixes into a small canonical form by removing trivially equivalent tokens (normalizing whitespace, templated slots, timestamp placeholders) and then emit a delta signature representing differences to an existing canonical. This lets near-identical prefixes map to the same canonical entry.
3) Shared ephemeral KV slices: materialize a single KV slice on GPU for the canonical prefix and let decoding sessions reference it with refcounts; session-specific deltas are applied via small overlay buffers (<< 1MB) rather than full duplication.
4) Eviction & hysteresis: implement hysteresis for eviction to avoid thrashing (keep recently coalesced entries for N batches and use access-weighted TTL).

Performance targets:
- Reduce GPU memory used for prefix materialization by >=25% on clustered-prefix workloads
- Reduce end-to-end per-request token cost by >=10% in production-like mixes
- No tail-latency regression beyond 5% for p99s when enabled

Risks & mitigations:
- Incorrect canonicalization could change model outputs. Mitigate by: 1) conservative normalization rules in v1 (whitespace, known templating markers only); 2) canary on low-impact routes; 3) golden prompt test suite against baseline to catch regressions.
- Prefetch can waste bandwidth/capacity when mispredicted. Mitigate: budget prefetch workers per GPU and add notion of prefetch score threshold.
- Reference counting complexity across multi-tenant memory scopes. Mitigate: first build as single-tenant per-pool prototype and only generalize after stability.

Acceptance criteria:
- Design doc reviewed and approved (link in links).
- Prototype integrated into continuous-batching path behind feature flag.
- Automated regression matrix (100+ prompts) run nightly showing zero semantic regressions for opt-in routes.
- Bench harness showing memory/token cost wins on at least two internal workloads.

Deliverables:
- Design doc (confluence), prototype PR, benchmark dashboard, rollout playbook, feature flag + circuit breaker, and monitoring (cost/latency/quality impact).
